clue.text: Unfair trying to link good chap in power with bounder

parts.note: a kangaroo is an animal that bounds along

indicators.note: the good chap sits inside the word for power, enclosed by it

parts.note: juice is slang for electric power
ST, saint, is the crossword's good person

explanation.surface: Someone complains of an unjust hearing that links a decent fellow in authority with a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like the old word for a cad, but here it is literally a leaping animal. A kangaroo court is a sham trial, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court dispenses rough, biased justice, so the phrase describes an unfair trial.

clue.text: Extremely kindly, wrapping ailing Jack with old wet blanket

indicators.note: the outer letters of kindly go round the rest, wrapping them
the extremes of the word kindly are its first and last letters

parts.note: ailing means ill
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A very kind person looks after a sick sailor alongside an old bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a person who dampens fun, the very meaning of a spoilsport.

clue.text: Famous tree oddly bathed in green light

indicators.note: the odd letters of tree are bathed in, surrounded by, the go-ahead

parts.note: a nod is a signal of approval, a green light

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word tree

explanation.surface: A celebrated tree is strangely lit by green light.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted is a synonym of famous, both meaning well known.

clue.text: It's smart killing a creature that's hard to catch

parts.note: something fast is quick and difficult to catch
a buck is a male deer or rabbit, a creature

explanation.surface: A hunter says it is clever to kill an elusive animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killing' is not slaughter but a big financial gain; 'smart' means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a fast buck is earning money quickly, a swift financial killing.

clue.text: Lower head in blood-soaked riot

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is moved lower down, the head dropping

parts.note: gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: Heads are lowered in a bloody riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower head' moves the first letter G of GORY down to the end, giving ORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot can mean a wild revel or excess, like an orgy of indulgence.

clue.text: One in rising company stops German's agreed influence

indicators.note: the company plugs, stops up, a gap between the other pieces

parts.note: ja is German for yes, agreed
bite means effect or influence, as when a policy has bite

explanation.surface: Someone joins a firm on the rise, halting a German-approved influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rising' is a rebellion: the Jacobite risings of 1715 and 1745 tried to restore the Stuart line.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacobite was a participant in the Stuart rebellions known as the Jacobite risings.

clue.text: One seeing future is reflecting on past line

indicators.note: reflecting turns the little word is back to front, as in a mirror

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by

explanation.surface: A fortune teller looks back on a fine past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the reversed piece before the rest in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world who foretold what was to come.

clue.text: Acting together on stage?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means jointly, and also literally performing at a musical show.

clue.text: Does out old naval officer's quarters

parts.note: ex means former, old
PO is a petty officer, with the possessive giving S
E and S are two quarters, compass points

explanation.surface: A former navy man's lodgings are searched.
explanation.definitionFit: To out someone is to reveal their secret, which is to lay them bare.

clue.text: A girl the different clubs become reluctant to move

indicators.note: made different, these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A girl at a different golf club becomes sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic describes someone sluggish and lacking energy, unwilling to stir.

clue.text: Roughly gatecrashing inn back in Lancashire town

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
the approximation barges into the pub like an uninvited guest

parts.note: a pub is an inn
CA, circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: Rowdy people burst into a pub back in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrashing' makes PUCAB, which 'back' reverses. Bacup is a small town in Lancashire, north-west England; 'Roughly' looks like an adverb on the gatecrashing but is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a market town in the Rossendale valley of Lancashire, England.

clue.text: Martial art mostly random hit and miss

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: judo is a Japanese martial art

indicators.note: random says the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Martial arts practice is a hit-and-miss affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the O of JUDO; 'random' rearranges HIT to ITH. 'Miss' is a girl, not a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith is a girl's name, and a miss is a young woman.

clue.text: Like to eat rubbish endlessly and seafood

indicators.note: the word for like takes the rest inside, eating it

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: baloney means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone likes junk food without end, plus fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the final Y of the word for rubbish; 'Like' is not a verb here but the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalones are edible sea molluscs, prized as seafood.

clue.text: You may underperform, portrayed as heartless operatic heroine

indicators.note: heartless strips the middle of each word, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A singer is told she may perform poorly and be shown as a cold heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Yum-Yum is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: Yum-Yum is the leading lady of the comic opera The Mikado.

clue.text: Run Jamaica rum — caught dropping drug

indicators.note: rum means odd, so the letters are rearranged
dropping says one letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Jamaican rum runner is caught dropping drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C from RUN JAMAICA and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Marijuana is cannabis, a recreational drug.

clue.text: London park and thoroughfare very untidy when judge visits

indicators.note: the judge drops in, going inside the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
in a mess means very untidy, so a mess fits

explanation.surface: A park and road in London are a mess when a judge comes by.
explanation.walkthrough: St James's Park is a royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: St James's Park is one of the royal parks in the heart of London.

clue.text: One putting energy into X-rated sin?

definitions.text: One putting energy into X-rated sin?

parts.note: adult describes X-rated material

indicators.note: into places the energy inside the word for sin

parts.note: to err is to sin
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cheat puts effort into an indecent sin.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer commits the sin of adultery, an adult misdeed.

clue.text: What cattle go through, circling near African city

indicators.note: the lowing sound goes round the abbreviation, circling it

parts.note: cattle go moo
via means through

explanation.surface: Cattle are herded past a town in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Monrovia is the capital city of Liberia in West Africa.

clue.text: Countered blows to the ear, finding a safe place

indicators.note: to the ear means the words are to be heard, not read

parts.note: fought knocks means resisted blows

explanation.surface: A boxer parries punches and finds refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Fort Knox in Kentucky holds the US gold reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Knox houses the US gold bullion depository, a byword for a secure vault.

clue.text: I forbid tearing of tissue

indicators.note: tearing rips the letters apart and rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone forbids tearing a tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibroid is a benign growth of fibrous tissue.

clue.text: Grand American cheers very small Swede, perhaps

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
ta is British for thanks, cheers
V is the abbreviation for very, made small

explanation.surface: A grand American toasts a tiny Swede.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav is a Swedish name, borne by several Swedish kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav is a Swedish forename, so a Swede might bear it.

clue.text: Driver on a landau keeping one in a draught?

indicators.note: keeping says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A coachman keeps someone in a cold draught.
explanation.walkthrough: The draught is a sleeping draught, not cold air.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronal was a barbiturate taken as a sleeping draught.

clue.text: In Ireland my drinks are spiked with punch

indicators.note: the drinks are spiked, with the punch put inside

parts.note: beers are drinks
jab is a punch

explanation.surface: In Ireland, drinks are laced with a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise; begorra and bejabers are Irish versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bejabers is an Irish exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'.

clue.text: UK carrier bags inflamed Dutch town

indicators.note: bags means holds inside, as in a bag

parts.note: BA is British Airways
inflamed skin is red

explanation.surface: A British airline flies inflamed bags to a Dutch town.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is a city in the south of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Old actor not allowing women to go with leading lady

parts.note: a stag party is men only
ER is the Queen, a leading lady

explanation.surface: A veteran actor refuses to let women accompany the star.
explanation.walkthrough: An old stager is a veteran; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A stager is an experienced performer, from the phrase old stager.

clue.text: A bit of Greek language book never gets right

indicators.note: never gets right says no letter for right is left

parts.note: a grammar is a book about a language

explanation.surface: A Greek textbook never gets things correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Rs (for right) are removed from GRAMMAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, so a small piece of Greek.

clue.text: Who speculates will also ultimately generate capital

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A speculator will also make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Speaker may appeal to class

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O Lord
rate means class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A speaker may plead with a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Orating is what a public speaker does, delivering a speech.

clue.text: Short Mystery plays in verse an official found in church

indicators.note: plays says the letters are moved about
short means a letter is cut off the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mystery plays in verse are performed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last Y from Mystery, leaving MYSTER; with V those letters are rearranged by 'plays' into VESTRYM, and AN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman is a member of a parish vestry, a church official.

clue.text: Like one driven through entrance, far from quick!

definitions.meaning: like a nail hammered into a door
quick means alive, so far from it means utterly dead

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means completely dead, as lifeless as a nail in a door.
